text:
sophie_pm: quick sync on private deploy roadmap 1 - packaging + upgrades. field asks keep coming for near-zero-downtime upgrades and IP continuity. want to pick a default upgrade lane and a documented backstop/"escape" option. thoughts?

tarun_eng: agree. i see 4 viable lanes now: in-place operator, rolling with sticky-ip, tenant blue/green with routing handoff, and cold forklift. each has tradeoffs re: infra cost, rollout complexity, and customer netops burden.

anya_neteng: from netops side, two hard constraints we keep hearing:
- preserve egress IP for permit-list customers
- avoid tearing down BGP sessions or changing ASN-handshakes mid-upgrade
if those are soft requirements, we can be flexible.

mike_sales: they are not soft for some customers. ACME and HealthSys will only accept upgrades that keep IPs; they'll pay for that as a premium SLA.

sophie_pm: proposal: pick tenant blue/green with routing handoff as "primary zero-downtime lane" and define a "network-preserve backstop" that uses a small-forwarding proxy for the upgrade window. backstop must be usable when customers cannot change their external routing quickly.

tarun_eng: ok. implementation sketch for the backstop:
```
- controller creates tenant upgrade session
- deploy ephemeral forwarders per node (DaemonSet) that can SNAT/keepalive connections
- update routing so new pods take traffic, but forwarder preserves outbound source via DNAT or HW offload
- fallback to SNAT with per-tenant mapping if HW NAT missing
```

anya_neteng: important: SNAT fallback breaks permit lists. backstop must include a managed IP mapping doc and a toggle for customers to opt-in after confirming firewall changes. also need per-tenant audit logs and KMS-encrypted keys for ephemeral mappings.

sec_bot: security-check: any network-forwarder introduces attack surface. require threat model, signed config bundles (kms), and e2e logging before GA. i'll open a ticket.

nora_cs: add acceptance criteria: clear list of supported topologies, minimum kernel/netstack features required, telemetry to show no packet loss > 1s, and an operator-level dry-run mode for customers. also include sample customer comms templates.

mike_sales: timeline ask from field: can we give a quarter estimate? customers want to know when they can buy the SLA.

tarun_eng: rough: spike for prototype forwarder (2 weeks), operator changes for routing handoff + sticky-ip (4 weeks), pilot validation with two customers (3 weeks). optimistic around 9 weeks if prioritized.

sophie_pm: action list:
- sophie: draft tradeoff + pricing options and publish to docs (due Thu)
- tarun: perf/security spike for forwarder PoC (demo in 2 weeks)
- anya: network capability matrix by customer tier + allowed workarounds (due Wed)
- sec_bot: create threat-model ticket and checklist (by Fri)
- nora: customer runbook + comms templates (due Thu)

anya_neteng: one more ask 1 for on-prem airgapped installs we need an operator bundle that doesn't call home during cutover. how does the backstop work without external HW NAT? tarun?

tarun_eng: for airgap: forwarder can run in pure-pod mode and maintain mapping via controller CRDs; we document limitations: on-prem backstop requires customer to provide an egress IP or accept a short permit-list window. will include in acceptance criteria.

sophie_pm: good. i'll fold airgap notes into the draft. if no objections i'll lock this choice as the recommended path and start comms to field. ping me if you want scope adjusted. :rocket:
